Window teardown uses :q or :bwipeout!, not scrollbind.

M13.BEB.P01.prompt:
ANIMATION
The first, middle, and third material clusters receive one-cell marks; both support rows remain exact.

    BEFORE           AFTER
    │| aa bb cc |│   │| aa bb cc |│

M13.BEB.P01.neovim_prompt:
NEOVIM
Why is B the final boundary step after the counted 2W?
M13.BEB.P01.neovim_answer: After 2W reaches the third cluster, B returns to the preceding middle-cluster WORD start so r+ marks that cluster in place.
choices: ANIMATION: All three middle-row clusters change; supports stay exact. | NEOVIM: B returns one WORD start after 2W, then r+ marks the middle cluster.
ANIMATION: The spaces collapse between clusters. | NEOVIM: B deletes the gap before r+.
ANIMATION: Support rows change with the middle row. | NEOVIM: B moves vertically to the lower row.
ANIMATION: Only the first cluster changes. | NEOVIM: B repeats the original W start instead of returning.
compact_choices: A: three clusters · V: B back one WORD, then r+
A: gaps collapse · V: B deletes gap
A: supports change · V: B moves down
A: first only · V: B repeats W
feedback: Correct: B returns one WORD start after 2W so the middle cluster can be edited in place.
B is motion, not deletion; cluster spacing remains fixed.
B stays on the acting row and does not select a support row.
The first cluster was already handled; B supplies the middle-cluster return.
